question: Which Indian state has its own constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: Nagaland
Sikkim
Jammu and Kashmir
Goa
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Jammu and Kashmir

Explanation:
Jammu and Kashmir was the only Indian state that had its own constitution. It came into effect in 1957 and granted special status to the state. Under Article 370, Jammu and Kashmir had the power to make laws separate from the Indian Constitution. However, on 5 August 2019, Article 370 was abrogated, and the state was reorganized into two union territories under the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act. Now, no Indian state has its own separate constitution. Other options like Nagaland, Sikkim, and Goa are governed solely under the Indian Constitution.

question: Who is the first citizen of India? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: Chief Justice of India
President of India
prime minister of India
Chief of the Indian Army
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President of India

Explanation:
According to Article 52 of the Indian Constitution, the President is the first citizen of India and the constitutional head of the nation. The President is also the Supreme Commander of the Indian Armed Forces. The President is elected by an Electoral College consisting of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and the Legislative Assemblies of states. The President is part of the Union Executive and exercises powers on the advice of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers. The Chief Justice, Prime Minister, or Chief of Army Staff are not the first citizen. The President symbolizes the unity and integrity of the country.

☛ What is the tenure of the President? → 5 years

☛ Who can impeach the President? → Parliament
☛ Who was the first President of India? → Dr. Rajendra Prasad

question: When did the Constitution of India come into force? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: January 1, 1950
26 January, 1950
26 November, 1949
26 January, 1949
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 26 January, 1950

Explanation:
The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26 November 1949, but it came into force on 26 January 1950. This date was chosen to commemorate the declaration of Purna Swaraj (complete independence) by the Indian National Congress in 1930. With the enforcement of the Constitution, India became a republic, and Dr. Rajendra Prasad became the first President of India. The original Constitution had 395 articles, 8 schedules, and 22 parts. Currently, there are 12 schedules. 26 January is celebrated as Republic Day in India.

question: In which year was the 'No Confidence Motion' introduced for the first time in the Lok Sabha? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: 1960
1973
1962
1963
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1963

Explanation:
The first No Confidence Motion in the Lok Sabha was introduced in the year 1963. It was moved against the then Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru but was subsequently rejected. A No Confidence Motion is a crucial tool in parliamentary democracy, allowing the opposition to express lack of confidence in the government. Under Article 75 of the Constitution, the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. Such a motion can only be introduced in the Lok Sabha, not in the Rajya Sabha. If passed, the government must resign.

question: Who among the following served as President for two consecutive terms? (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: Dr. Rajendra Prasad
Dr. S. Radhakrishnan
Shri V.V. Giri
A P J Abdul Kalam
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Dr. Rajendra Prasad

Explanation:
Dr. Rajendra Prasad was the first President of India and the only one to serve two consecutive terms (1950-1962). He assumed office after the adoption of the Indian Constitution in 1950 and was re-elected in 1957. Dr. S. Radhakrishnan (1962-1967) and V.V. Giri (1969-1974) served only one term each. A P J Abdul Kalam (2002-2007) also served a single term. Dr. Prasad played a key role in the Indian independence movement and the Constituent Assembly.

question: The Indian constitution provides for _______. (RPF SI 2018 (19/12/2018) Shift 3)
options: neither
single citizenship
Both
dual citizenship
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is single citizenship

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution provides for single citizenship, meaning all citizens have a uniform citizenship across the entire country. This differs from federal countries like the USA, which have dual citizenship (state and national). The provisions for citizenship are covered in Part II (Articles 5-11) of the Indian Constitution. Single citizenship promotes national unity and prevents discrimination between states. It ensures that all citizens enjoy equal rights throughout the country. Unlike some federal nations, India does not have separate citizenship for states, thus strengthening the idea of one nation.

question: What is written in Article 1 of the Indian Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (24/12/2018) Shift 1)
options: India will be a federal republic
India i.e. Bharat will be a single state
India i.e. Bharat will be a union of states
India i.e. Bharat will be a federation of states
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is India i.e. Bharat will be a union of states

Explanation:
Article 1 states that India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States. The term 'Union' was deliberately chosen over 'Federation' to emphasize the indestructible nature of the Indian Union. Unlike a federation, states have no right to secede. This article is part of Part I of the Constitution (Articles 1 to 4), which deals with the Union and its territory. It declares the official names of the country as India and Bharat. The provision ensures that the Union is indestructible and the states are created or abolished only by the Parliament. Article 1 lays the foundation for India's federal structure with a unitary bias.

☛ Is India a federation? → No, it is a union of states

question: Where is the High Court of Uttar Pradesh located? (RPF SI 2018 (24/12/2018) Shift 1)

Explanation:

The jurisdiction of the High Court extends over the entire state of Uttar Pradesh. It functions under the Indian Constitution and hears civil and criminal cases within its jurisdiction. Being one of the oldest high courts, it has a rich history and has delivered many landmark judgments. The court consists of a Chief Justice and several other judges appointed by the President of India. Its efficient functioning ensures justice and upholds the rule of law in the state.

question: Which type of government system has been adopted in the Indian Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (24/12/2018) Shift 1)

Presidential

Aristocracy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Parliamentary

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution has adopted a Parliamentary system of government, which is based on the British model. In this system, the President is the constitutional head, while the Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers are the real executive heads. The executive is accountable to the legislature in the parliamentary system. India has a bicameral legislature consisting of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha. The Prime Minister is appointed by the President, and the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha. This system ensures government stability and democratic accountability.

President of India

Explanation:

question: How many schedules are there at present in the Indian Constitution? (RPF SI 2018 (24/12/2018) Shift 1)
options: 8

10
12
solution:

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution currently has 12 schedules. Originally, there were 8 schedules, increased through amendments. The First Schedule lists states and union territories; the Second deals with salaries of President, Governors, etc. The Third contains oaths and affirmations. The Fourth allocates Rajya Sabha seats. Fifth and Sixth relate to administration of Scheduled Tribes. The Seventh has Union, State, and Concurrent lists. Eighth includes languages. Ninth covers land reform laws. Tenth is the anti-defection law. Eleventh deals with Panchayati Raj, and Twelfth with municipalities. These schedules provide detailed structures for governance and rights.

भारत के मुख्य चुनाव आयुक्त (CEC) का कार्यकाल संविधान के अनुच्छेद 324 के तहत निर्धारित है। CEC का कार्यकाल 6 वर्ष या 65 वर्ष की आयु तक, जो भी पहले हो, रहता है। यह प्रावधान चुनाव आयोग की स्वतंत्रता सुनिश्चित करने के लिए बनाया गया है। CEC की नियुक्ति राष्ट्रपति द्वारा की जाती है और उन्हें केवल महाभियोग द्वारा ही हटाया जा सकता है। यह कार्यकाल सीमा सुनिश्चित करती है कि CEC अपने पद पर अधिकतम छह वर्ष या 65 वर्ष की आयु तक ही रह सकते हैं, जिससे युवा प्रतिभाओं को अवसर मिलता है और निष्पक्ष चुनाव सुनिश्चित होते हैं। अन्य विकल्पों में दी गई अवधि (जैसे 5 वर्ष या 70 वर्ष) सही नहीं हैं क्योंकि संवैधानिक प्रावधान 6 वर्ष या 65 वर्ष ही हैं।

question: Articles 36 to 51 containing 'Directive Principles of State Policy' come under which Part of the Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Part V
Part II
Part III
Part IV
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Part IV

Explanation:
The Part IV of the Indian Constitution (Articles 36 to 51) contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP). These principles are inspired by the Irish Constitution and guide the state in making policies. They are non-justiciable, meaning they cannot be enforced by courts, yet they are fundamental in governance. Their goal is to establish social and economic justice and move towards a welfare state. Part III (Articles 12-35) deals with Fundamental Rights, Part V with the Union Executive and Legislature, and Part II with Citizenship.

question_hi: 'राज्य नीति के निदेशक सिद्धांत' वाले अनुच्छेद 36 से 51 संविधान के किस भाग के अंतर्गत आते हैं? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:
भारतीय संविधान के भाग IV में अनुच्छेद 36 से 51 तक राज्य नीति के निदेशक सिद्धांत (DPSP) शामिल हैं। ये सिद्धांत आयरलैंड के संविधान से प्रेरित हैं और राज्य को नीतियाँ बनाने में मार्गदर्शन देते हैं। ये न्यायोचित नहीं हैं, अर्थात इन्हें न्यायालय में लागू नहीं किया जा सकता, फिर भी ये शासन में मौलिक हैं। इनका उद्देश्य सामाजिक और आर्थिक न्याय स्थापित करना तथा कल्याणकारी राज्य की ओर ले जाना है। भाग III (अनुच्छेद 12-35) मौलिक अधिकारों से संबंधित है, जबकि भाग V संघ कार्यपालिका और विधायिका से। भाग II नागरिकता से संबंधित है।

question: Which Directive Principle of State Policy focuses on the provision of just and humane conditions for work? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 50
Article 51
Article 42
Article 47
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 42

Explanation:
Article 42 of the Indian Constitution directs the State to make provision for just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief. This is a key Directive Principle of State Policy (DPSP) focused on labor welfare. Article 42 aims to prevent exploitation of workers and ensure dignified living conditions. question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution outlines the allocation of seats in the Council of States? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)

Fourth Schedule
Sixth Schedule

The Fourth Schedule of the Indian Constitution deals with the allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) to the states and union territories. question: The Swaran Singh Committee recommendation added which of the following to the Indian Constitution? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Fundamental Rights
Preamble
Fundamental Duties
Directive Principles of State Policy
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Fundamental Duties

Explanation:
The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended the inclusion of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution. Consequently, the 42nd Amendment (1976) added Part IV-A containing Article 51A, which lists 11 fundamental duties for citizens. These duties reflect moral and civic obligations, such as defending the nation, protecting public property, and developing scientific temper. The committee was chaired by the then Law Minister Swaran Singh. Fundamental Duties were not part of the original Constitution but were added later. They apply only to citizens, not to foreigners.

question: According to the Constitution of India, who conducts the Election of the Vice-President of India? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: The Election Commission of India
The Parliament of India
The Legislature Councils of all States
The Legislative Assemblies of all States
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Election Commission of India

Explanation:
According to Article 66 of the Indian Constitution, the election of the Vice-President is conducted and controlled by the Election Commission of India. The election is held through the system of single transferable vote, where the electorate consists of members of both Houses of Parliament. The Election Commission issues the notification, receives nominations, ensures the process of voting and counting. The Vice-President holds office for a term of five years and serves as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha. The Election Commission is an independent constitutional body that ensures free and fair elections.

question: Which of the following Articles of the Constitution was amended to include the Right to Education as a Fundamental Right? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 30
Article 21
Article 18
Article 19
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 21

Explanation:
The Right to Education was originally a Directive Principle under Article 45 in Part IV of the Constitution. The 86th Constitutional Amendment Act (2002) made it a Fundamental Right by inserting Article 21A after Article 21. Article 21A provides free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years. It is an extension of Article 21 (Right to Life). This right was enforced through the Right to Education Act, 2009. Hence, the correct answer is Article 21.

solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है अनुच्छेद 21

Explanation:
शिक्षा का अधिकार मूल रूप से संविधान के भाग IV (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्वों) में अनुच्छेद 45 के अंतर्गत था। 86वें संविधान संशोधन (2002) द्वारा इसे मौलिक अधिकार बनाया गया। इस संशोधन ने अनुच्छेद 21 के बाद अनुच्छेद 21A जोड़ा, जो 6-14 वर्ष के बच्चों को मुफ्त और अनिवार्य शिक्षा का अधिकार देता है। अनुच्छेद 21A को 'शिक्षा का अधिकार' कहा जाता है और यह अनुच्छेद 21 (जीवन के अधिकार) का विस्तार है। यह अधिकार RTE Act, 2009 के माध्यम से लागू हुआ। इस प्रकार, सही उत्तर अनुच्छेद 21 है।
